findings.where: The 'Vibe' section heading, desktop and phone
findings.fault: The 'Vibe' heading looks like a link: it is italic, turquoise and underlined, while 'Surf' and 'Good for' are plain ink headings. Clicking it does nothing (parts map p5: static). The underline and the link colour belong to links. It is also the only heading styled this way, so it looks like a mistake. The text is set in raw turquoise, which DESIGN.md allows only as a fill, not as type.
findings.who_objects: The backpacker, who taps it expecting more about the vibe and gets nothing, then stops trusting which underlines are real links. The founder too, since the brand bars raw fill colours as text.

findings.where: The 'Good for' tag row (the 12 pills, from 'First-time surfers' to 'Sunsets'), desktop and phone
findings.fault: Each tag is a heavy pill with a thick border, coloured like a button or a filter chip. Clicking any of them does nothing (parts map p6–p17: static). The colours, rotating yellow, green, pink, blue, purple and magenta, carry no meaning. Several aren't in the palette at all, and amber is reserved for rewards. In a calm reading area, this row is the loudest thing on the page.
findings.who_objects: The backpacker, who taps 'Budget' or 'Solo travellers' expecting to filter hostels and nothing happens. The brand owner too, since DESIGN.md says colour that carries no information does not appear in the working area, and each colour has one job.

findings.where: The 'coming soon' announcement box above the footer, desktop and phone
findings.fault: A neutral notice ('listings coming soon') sits on a saturated red block, the colour of an error or a warning. It is the strongest colour on the page, so the page seems to end on an alarm. DESIGN.md puts the interior announcement on the ink night ground, and red is kept for danger and sold-out. On desktop the text fills only the left half of a full-width red box, so it looks unfinished.
findings.who_objects: The backpacker, who at first glance reads it as 'something is wrong' or 'unavailable'. The founder too, since the brand names the announcement's ground and keeps semantic red for errors.

findings.where: The page title 'Best Hostels in Canggu' compared with what the page holds
findings.fault: The heading promises a list of the best hostels, but the page names no hostel. The visitor learns there are no listings only from the last block before the footer. The heading is also in title case, against the brand's sentence case.
findings.who_objects: The backpacker arriving from search for 'best hostels in Canggu', who reads the whole page waiting for hostels, feels misled and goes back to a booking site. The founder too, since honesty is a product principle and a misleading heading costs search trust.

findings.where: Nav 'Destinations' and 'How we rank'; footer 'Privacy', 'Terms', 'How we rank' and 'Report content'
findings.fault: 'Destinations' points to #destinations, but this page has no such section. 'How we rank' (in the nav and the footer), 'Privacy', 'Terms' and 'Report content' all point back to this same page. Every navigation link except the email goes nowhere.
findings.who_objects: The backpacker, who wants to compare Canggu with Uluwatu or Lombok, or to check how the ranking works before trusting it, and finds every link dead. Anyone checking the privacy or legal pages finds none.

findings.where: The whole page, read as a next step for the visitor
findings.fault: The page is a dead end. There are no listings, no way to be told when they arrive, and no link to other Bali or Lombok areas. The visitor leaves with no action.
findings.who_objects: The backpacker, who is choosing where to stay now and has nowhere to go but another site. The founder too, who loses the visitor for good at launch.

findings.fault: The section that does the page's job (what to look for in a hostel here) gets the smallest heading on the page: a small, letter-spaced uppercase label. Surf, Vibe and Good for get full headings. The order of importance is upside down, and the uppercase breaks the brand's casing rule.
findings.who_objects: The backpacker scanning for hostel advice, who skims past it as a caption.

findings.where: Body text in every section: intro, Surf, Vibe, What to look for and the announcement, worst on phone
findings.fault: The body text is justified, which opens wide gaps between words. On phone the announcement's first line reads 'MantaHostels   is   launching   across', and the intro's 'workers   and   long-stay' has rivers too.
findings.who_objects: The phone reader, the primary user, for whom uneven gaps slow reading and make the page look poorly made.

findings.fault: The text runs in a narrow left column and leaves the right 60% of the screen empty. Meanwhile the tag row and the red box run full width, so the page has no consistent edge and looks half built. A destination page's top banner is meant to be the loud zone, but there is no hero, image or illustration, so the first screen is plain text on sand.
findings.who_objects: The backpacker on a laptop, whose first impression is a bare, unfinished page rather than a beachy travel brand. The founder too, whose brand names 'sterile' as the enemy and puts a loud banner at the top of destination pages.

findings.fault: Twelve tags cover nearly every kind of traveller (first-time surfers, couples, solo travellers, budget, nightlife, yoga, remote workers). A list that fits everyone doesn't help anyone decide whether Canggu suits them.
findings.who_objects: The backpacker comparing Canggu with other areas, who learns nothing from the tags that sets Canggu apart.
